subject.title: Agent-created crons inherit session toolsAllow at create-time; patch toolsAllow:null is a silent no-op; claude-cli backend then refuses the job

question: Should an explicit or legacy flagless `toolsAllow` incompatibility on a claude-cli fallback candidate fail the whole cron run, or skip only that candidate while preserving fail-closed enforcement?
rationale: The current hard failure preserves the tool-policy boundary but can disable recurring jobs even when another fallback candidate could enforce the restriction; changing this requires an explicit decision about fallback semantics at a security boundary.

options.title: Fail over safely
options.body: Classify the CLI capability mismatch as permanent and non-auth, skip that candidate, and retain the restriction for any subsequent enforceable runtime.

options.title: Reject before scheduling
options.body: Reject creation or update when the selected runtime is already known to be an incompatible CLI backend, accepting that later provider fallback changes can still expose the mismatch.

options.title: Keep whole-run failure
options.body: Retain the current hard failure and limit the change to clearer agent-tool errors and operator diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Fail over safely
recommendation.body: Classify the CLI capability mismatch as permanent and non-auth, skip that candidate, and retain the restriction for any subsequent enforceable runtime.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work most directly defines the current distinction between inherited defaults, explicit restrictions, and CLI execution behavior.
